title: How a swimming pool is built (cutaway)

beats.text: An empty swimming pool can float right out of the ground.
beats.shot: Cutaway of the finished, drained pool. Groundwater rises in the soil and the whole concrete shell lifts out, cracking the deck.
beats.camera: slow push-in on the section, low and centered

beats.text: So how do you build one that stays put?
beats.shot: Freeze, then the whole build plays backwards to bare lawn.

beats.text: It starts with a hole. An excavator digs out about fifty tons of soil.
beats.shot: Excavator behind the cut bites the lawn; soil columns drop away in section; spoil pile grows.
beats.camera: wide establishing side view, slow drift right

beats.text: Underground, it's layers: topsoil, clay, sand, and then groundwater.
beats.shot: Strata labels pop up on the section face; the water table glows blue at the bottom.
beats.camera: glide down the section face from grass to groundwater

beats.text: So the floor gets gravel, to let that water drain away.
beats.shot: Gravel spreads across the floor of the hole, seen in section.

beats.text: A relief valve in the floor opens if groundwater pushes up, so water comes in, instead of lifting the pool.
beats.shot: Relief valve set into the floor; arrows show water pushing up through it.
beats.camera: close-up on the valve in section

beats.text: Then the plumbing: a drain at the bottom, a skimmer at the top, jets in the walls.
beats.shot: Transparent pipes appear in the section, running from drain and skimmer to the equipment pad.
beats.camera: follow the pipe path from the drain to the pad

beats.text: Next, a cage of steel rebar, with a bar every twenty-five centimeters.
beats.shot: Rebar grid builds bar by bar over floor and walls.
beats.camera: slow orbit-like slide along the hole

beats.text: Concrete is sprayed on at high speed, twenty centimeters thick.
beats.shot: Shell grows over the rebar; dimension line shows the 20 cm wall in section.

beats.text: It cures for four weeks, and gets watered every day so it doesn't crack.
beats.shot: Day-night time-lapse over the cutaway; sprinkler mist each morning.

beats.text: Then tiles, stone coping, and smooth plaster to seal it.
beats.shot: Tile band, coping and plaster layer appear; plaster thickness visible in section.

beats.text: It's filled right away: fresh plaster cures best underwater. Twenty thousand liters.
beats.shot: Water rises in section; fill gauge counts up.

beats.text: Twenty tons of water now hold it down. It stays put.
beats.shot: Down arrows on the water vs up arrows from the groundwater; the down arrows win.
beats.camera: pull back to show the whole section

beats.text: To stay clean, water flows from the skimmer and drain, through a pump and filter, and back out the jets.
beats.shot: Flow stripes run through the transparent pipes: drain/skimmer → pump → filter → jets.
beats.camera: follow the flow along the pipes

beats.text: The whole pool passes through that filter about every six hours.
And that's why you should never drain a pool after a week of heavy rain.
beats.shot: Back to the hook angle; rain falls; water table rises toward the pool.
beats.camera: settle on the hook framing (loops into the opening)
